title: dira check --json
description: The machine-readable verdict of `dira check`. This is a published contract: a pre-commit hook, a CI step or a coding agent parses it to decide whether a plan contradicts something the ledger already settled. The exit code is the primary signal (0 compliant, 2 at least one cited conflict, 1 dira's own error) and is repeated here so a caller holding only stdout still knows what it is looking at. Two rules below are security rules rather than shape rules, and are expressed as schema constraints so that a leak fails validation rather than review: a private entry is cited by reference and never by text (cst-0003), and no basis other than an alternative may carry a revisit condition, because entry.schema.json gives `revisit_if` only to `$defs/alternative` (docs/design.md §7).

plan.description: The candidate text that was checked, as it was given.

verdict.description: Whether the plan contradicts anything the ledger enforces.

exit_code.description: The process exit code this verdict produced. 1 is dira's own failure and never appears in a document, because a run that failed produced no verdict to serialise.

enforced_entries.description: How many entries were eligible to be cited. Reported because "no conflict" against a ledger the check failed to read is indistinguishable from "no conflict" against one it read in full, and only one of those is an answer.

conflicts.description: The citations, strongest first and then by entry id. The order is total, so two runs over the same ledger produce the same document.

ref.description: An entry reference, optionally namespaced by a ledger name. Matches the `$defs/ref` pattern in entry.schema.json.

kind.description: The kinds that are enforcement substrate. An intent, a question and a note are never matched independently.

state.description: The enforced states. A staged decision is an unconfirmed regex-tier guess and is never cited (dec-0003); a superseded entry is not enforced here.

date.description: When the entry last changed, or when it was created if it has not. Absent only for an entry whose record carries no usable timestamp.

private.description: True when the entry is cited by reference only. The rule is unconditional rather than context-dependent: the binary cannot classify its own stdout, because a pipe into a pull-request body looks exactly like a terminal.

basis.description: What inside the entry was matched: a road the decision did not take, a rejected decision's own subject, or a standing rule.

rejected_alternative.description: The `alternatives[].option` text the plan proposes again.

why_not.description: That alternative's recorded reason, whitespace-collapsed out of its YAML folded scalar.

revisit_if.description: The condition under which the door legitimately reopens. Null means none is recorded — and for a constraint or a rejected decision's own subject it is null always, because that kind has no field to carry one. Null is never "never": `supersede` is the remedy that always exists.

supersede.description: The entry to supersede, in writing, to change what is enforced. Always the cited entry.

score.description: The overlap that produced the citation, rounded to three decimals. Advisory: the verdict is already decided by the time a conflict exists, and this number moves whenever the matcher is retuned. Do not branch on it.

allOf.description: cst-0003: a private entry is cited by ref and never by text, in every mode including this one.
Only an alternative can carry a revisit condition or an option text.
A non-private alternative citation must quote what was proposed and why it was refused. A citation with neither is an assertion.
